problem.text: Let $N$ be the greatest integer multiple of $36$ all of whose digits are even and no two of whose digits are the same. Find the remainder when $N$ is divided by $1000$.

steps.title: Where to start: only five digits are available
steps.body: The even digits are $0, 2, 4, 6, 8$, and no digit may repeat, so $N$ has at most five digits. That makes the search small. Also $36 = 4\cdot 9$ with $4$ and $9$ sharing no factor, so $N$ must pass the divisibility tests for both $9$ and $4$.

your_turn.prompt: State the divisibility tests for $9$ and for $4$.
your_turn.answer: Divisible by $9$: the digit sum is a multiple of $9$. Divisible by $4$: the number formed by the last two digits is a multiple of $4$.

steps.title: Can $N$ have five digits?
steps.body: A five-digit number with distinct even digits must use all of $0, 2, 4, 6, 8$, in some order. The order does not change the digit sum.

your_turn.prompt: What is $0 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 8$, and is it a multiple of $9$?
your_turn.answer: It is $20$, which is not a multiple of $9$. So no five-digit number works.

steps.title: Drop one digit to fix the sum
steps.body: Any four-digit number is bigger than any number with three or fewer digits, so we look for four digits first. Dropping digit $d$ leaves sum $20 - d$, where $d$ is $0, 2, 4, 6$ or $8$. This sum is between $12$ and $20$, and the only multiple of $9$ in that range is $18$.

your_turn.prompt: Which digit must be dropped, and which four digits are left?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The largest arrangement of $0, 4, 6, 8$ puts the digits in decreasing order: $8640$. Its last two digits, $40$, form a multiple of $4$, and its digit sum is $18$, so $8640 = 36\cdot 240$. No larger arrangement exists, so $N = 8640$, and the remainder when divided by $1000$ is $640$. The answer is **$640$**.
